rationale: The replication ported the column-5 OLS earnings specifications (log weekly wage on education plus covariates and year-of-birth dummies) for prime-age men and tested the joint significance of the three added quarter-of-birth dummies. For the 1970 Census (men born 1920-1929, N=247199), step 2 (port_table4.R -> outputs/table4.json) produced qob_ftest_col5 F=0.4400631 on df1=3 with p=0.7243, matching the paper's 0.73 (0.8% relative error). For the 1980 Census (men born 1930-1939, N=329509), step 3 (port_table5.R -> outputs/table5.json) produced qob_ftest_col5 F=1.8280393 with p=0.1396, matching the paper's 0.13 (7.4% relative error, well within the 30% partial band and effectively at the 5% boundary; both are jointly-insignificant p-values conveying the same conclusion). The replication_log.json notes confirm the QOB dummies are jointly insignificant in the wage equation, consistent with the exclusion restriction. No critical fixes in fix_severity affect this code path; the recorded fixes were straightforward Stata-to-R ports.
